description: A subscriber letter in a beekeeper's voice (first person singular, contractions, no exclamation marks, no 'we') from three samples and notes: the harvest figures and last-pickup date are kept, the two lost hives are reported as unexplained (no cause invented), and the notes' internal remark about a neighbour stays out.
prompt: samples.md has three letters I sent to my honey subscribers, and notes.md has what happened this season. Write the October letter so it sounds like me, and save it to out/letter.md.

files.samples.md:
# Letters by Odile Brannock, Marrow Brook Apiary (written by her, sent to the subscriber list)

## Letter, April
The bees are out. All of them, as far as I can tell, which isn't the same as all of them being fine. I've lifted every lid once and I'm not doing it again until May; they didn't enjoy it, and neither did I.

Hive 3 is the loud one. I won't say more than that.

Odile

## Letter, June
I bottled the first honey on Sunday. It's pale and it tastes of clover, which is what I'd hoped for and not what I'd promised. Jars are on the porch shelf; the honesty box is the tin with the dent.

I've stopped apologising for the price. It's what it costs.

Odile

## Letter, August
Two hives swarmed. I watched one go and couldn't have stopped it if I'd tried. They're in a hedge two fields over and they're not my problem now, which is a lovely feeling.

The rest are heavy. I've been told that's good.

Odile
files.notes.md:
Notes for the October letter (Odile):
- Autumn harvest is done: 212 jars this year. Last year it was 168, so 44 more.
- I started the year with 14 hives and have 12 going into winter. Two were lost over the summer. Why, I don't know yet; nobody has looked at them.
- Jars are still $9 each.
- Last pickup day is Saturday 22 November, porch shelf, as usual.
- INTERNAL, do not write about this: the neighbour on the east side complained about the bees again and I'm thinking of moving hives 5 and 6. Nothing decided.

checks.note: the notes state the difference with last year (44 more, from 168); the letter keeps it as the difference or as last year's figure
the notes mark the neighbour remark as internal; it must not reach the subscribers
the notes say why the two hives were lost is not known; the letter must not supply a cause
the loss is reported as unexplained, in any wording
the two lost hives or the 12 that remain, as digits or words; 'Twelve hives are going into winter ... we lost two over summer' (run variant-iso r3) reports both
the samples never use an exclamation mark
the samples are first person singular
she runs the apiary alone in every sample

checks.pattern: \[(?:ASK AUTHOR|VERIFY|UNTESTED)\b|(?i:as requested|your notes|the notes|the samples|voice profile)
checks.note: the letter goes to subscribers: no gap markers and no narration about the notes inside it
the three samples run 43, 51 and 57 words, so a 56 to 59 word letter (runs skill r2, variant-iso r2/r3, baseline r3) matches their length; the floor only rules out a stub

controls.output:
The autumn harvest is done. I bottled 212 jars this year, which is 44 more than last year's 168, and I'm not convinced the bees know they've overachieved.

I started the year with 14 hives and I'm going into winter with 12. I lost two over the summer. I don't know why yet; nobody's looked at them, and I won't guess in a letter.

Jars are still $9. Last pickup day is Saturday 22 November, porch shelf, as usual.

Odile
